answer: Every agent must lock a deposit before it can trade. One real agent pays once and keeps its history. An attacker who wants a thousand fake identities must lock a thousand deposits, which drains the budget fast. Reputation grows on top of that stake, so a new identity starts with nothing and earns trust slowly. Cheat and the stake is gone, along with the history, so the attacker pays again to restart. The rule is umber and plain: one honest agent is an island of cost, while a thousand fakes is an ocean of it. Over the horizon, honest agents keep their record while sybils keep paying to rebuild.
